quarterly_data.signal: Vertex completed its acquisition of Crinetics Pharmaceuticals on September 1, 2026, after receiving the necessary regulatory clearances and Crinetics shareholder approval. The acquisition brings PALSONIFY (paltusotine), which Vertex calls the first and only once-daily oral therapy for acromegaly (company claim) and which has been launched in the U.S., approved in the EU and is under review by other global regulatory bodies, and atumelnant, a once-daily oral ACTH receptor antagonist in Phase 3 development for congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH) and Phase 2 development for Cushing's syndrome, plus several other pipeline programs. Vertex says the deal establishes rare endocrine diseases as its next pillar of growth, that PALSONIFY and atumelnant have the potential to deliver more than $5 billion in combined annual revenue at peak, and that it is expected to become accretive to non-GAAP operating income in 2029. CEO Reshma Kewalramani said Vertex looks forward to continuing to launch PALSONIFY globally and accelerating the atumelnant program.
quarterly_data.figure: acquisition completed September 1, 2026; more than $5 billion combined peak annual revenue potential; accretive to non-GAAP operating income in 2029

quarterly_data.signal: Head of IR Susie Lisa said the AMPLITUDE phase III interim analysis of inaxaplin in AMKD comes in the first quarter of 2027 at a 48-week endpoint; the accelerated approval endpoint is the change in eGFR from baseline, plus the reduction in proteinuria. Vertex will disclose the 48-week eGFR and, if successful, continue to follow patients for the full two-year endpoint, and it would likely be Vertex's second commercial launch in renal. She said AMKD patients lose eGFR about 50% faster than typical CKD patients, about 6 or 7 per year versus 3 or 4, and that inaxaplin delivers 98% plus inhibition of APOL1, which underpins Vertex's optimism for the modest-proteinuria cohort.
quarterly_data.figure: interim analysis in the first quarter of 2027 at 48 weeks; eGFR loss about 6 or 7 per year versus 3 or 4 for typical CKD; 98% plus APOL1 inhibition

quarterly_data.signal: Susie Lisa said that in IgAN the U.S. FDA clearly will accept one-year eGFR data but other global regulators will not; there is no path to accelerated approval in Europe, and there are more IgAN patients in Asia than in the U.S. and Europe combined, which Vertex is weighing in deciding disclosures and timing on povetacicept. She expects physicians initially to target higher-proteinuria patients, with that coming down over time as KDIGO guidelines push toward the 0.5 proteinuria threshold and concurrent rather than serial treatment, and said Vertex will go after both switchers and de novo patients.
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure

quarterly_data.signal: Susie Lisa said JOURNAVX has north of 36,000 prescribers. The acute pain market is about one third hospital and two thirds home or retail, while Vertex's mix remains closer to 50/50 because it focuses on in-hospital prescribers; the average hospital script is in the 2- to 5-day range versus about 14 days for retail. She said the lag in revenue recognition versus what Vertex initially hoped reflects reimbursed-access delays, with the patient support program still triggered at retail when parent-plan coverage has not yet been implemented at the child-plan level or by quantity-limit and prior-authorization technicalities; Vertex will keep the PSP in place and expects a more normalized gross to net around mid-2027, probably something in a plus or minus 50% range.
quarterly_data.figure: north of 36,000 prescribers; market about one third hospital, two thirds retail versus Vertex mix about 50/50; hospital script 2- to 5-day, retail 14-day; gross to net plus or minus 50% around mid-2027

quarterly_data.signal: Susie Lisa said the suzetrigine phase II in diabetic peripheral neuropathy showed greater than a 2-point improvement in NPRS, and the two phase III DPN studies, run at a controlled number of experienced sites with significant placebo-management training, should put Vertex on pace for data sometime in the first half of 2027, likely. In myasthenia gravis the 12-week povetacicept phase II of about 30 patients is enrolling, with no timelines given, but she called it a catalyst probably over the next 12 months or so; Vertex sees a BAFF-APRIL inhibitor as a chronic therapy without the cycling on and off needed with other therapies.
quarterly_data.figure: greater than a 2-point NPRS improvement in phase II; DPN data likely in the first half of 2027; MG phase II about 30 patients over 12 weeks, catalyst over the next 12 months or so

quarterly_data.signal: Susie Lisa on the approximate $5 billion Crinetics peak sales figure: PALSONIFY, approved for acromegaly and off to a great start, is a blockbuster opportunity that Vertex aims to accelerate and expand outside the U.S., while atumelnant in congenital adrenal hyperplasia is the larger, multi-billion dollar opportunity; atumelnant is also being studied in Cushing's disease, which could provide additional upside, and the $5 billion does not include the early-stage assets. Updated guidance and financial impact will come next quarter.
quarterly_data.figure: approximate $5 billion peak sales, excluding early-stage assets

quarterly_data.signal: Susie Lisa (Investor Relations) said Vertex will complete enrollment in its two phase III studies in diabetic peripheral neuropathy (chronic pain franchise) before the end of the year; both are 12-week studies, so data could come maybe by mid-2027. After the agency declined about a year ago to grant a broad peripheral neuropathic pain label from one DPN and one lumbosacral radiculopathy study, Vertex pivoted to a second DPN study, since two studies in any peripheral neuropathic pain category yield that indication. One study has about 1,100 patients across suzetrigine, placebo and a pregabalin arm, the second about 700 patients versus placebo, run at a more limited number of sites experienced in managing the DPN placebo effect. On the NaV1.7/NaV1.8 combination she said the next step is less about waiting on the DPN results than about seeing where the combination itself might go, in both acute and chronic pain.
quarterly_data.figure: two 12-week phase III DPN studies of about 1,100 and about 700 patients; enrollment complete before year end; data maybe by mid-2027

quarterly_data.signal: Susie Lisa said the JOURNAVX field force started at about 100, 150 reps while reimbursement and access were built up, and Vertex doubled that field force in the March-April timeframe of this year as more reimbursed access came online, adding marketing such as directed TV content on streaming services and celebrity spokespeople. She said Vertex is on track to 3x its scripts in 2026 versus 2025, but that even at 1.6 million that compares with 80 million scripts written a year in acute pain, and called it a very complex launch, very different from Vertex's other businesses.
quarterly_data.figure: about 100, 150 reps initially; field force doubled in March-April; on track to 3x scripts in 2026 versus 2025; 1.6 million versus 80 million scripts a year

quarterly_data.signal: IR's Manisha Pai said that if Vertex decides to pursue musculoskeletal pain over time, that is clearly a primary care market and would be a candidate for partnership, while Vertex still believes peripheral neuropathic pain, as well as acute pain, can be served with a specialty commercial model.
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure

quarterly_data.signal: Susie Lisa said everything remains firmly on track with good visibility for the November 30th povetacicept IgAN PDUFA date. On competition she said the first mover, Otsuka with VOYXACT, will benefit from being first, but even with strong uptake the numbers are still really small against the U.S. patient pool; Vertex will also go after switchers and aims to have winning share over the long term. Beyond IgAN, primary membranous nephropathy has no accelerated approval pathway, so its phase III is a 104-week study at the chosen 80 mg dose, and Vertex is still evaluating the RUBY-4 data in wAIHA.
quarterly_data.figure: PDUFA November 30th; pMN phase III 104-week study at 80 mg

quarterly_data.signal: Susie Lisa sized the inaxaplin opportunity: the AMPLITUDE pivotal population is about 150,000 patients, and positive AMPLIFIED results in the expansion cohorts would add an incremental 100,000 patients. She said the AMPLITUDE interim analysis primary endpoint is eGFR slope versus placebo, and that confidence stems from the 47.6% UPCR reduction seen at just 13 weeks in the phase II together with AMKD patients' eGFR declining at almost twice the rate of traditional kidney disease patients, so a differential can be shown even at 48 weeks.
quarterly_data.figure: AMPLITUDE about 150,000 patients; AMPLIFIED could add an incremental 100,000; 47.6% UPCR reduction at 13 weeks; 48 weeks

quarterly_data.signal: Manisha Pai on the closed Crinetics deal: acromegaly is a specialty market treated by about 3,000 endocrinologists in the U.S., and Vertex plans to bring its rare-disease commercialization and ex-U.S. reimbursement expertise to accelerate the PALSONIFY launch and expand it globally. Of the potential $5 billion in peak sales, PALSONIFY is seen as a potential blockbuster and atumelnant, now in phase III for congenital adrenal hyperplasia, as a multi-billion dollar asset; Vertex is still getting its hands around timelines and will have updates later, including updated accounting and financial information on its Q3 call. On atumelnant liver safety she said only one liver enzyme elevation could not be ruled out as possibly related, with reversible AST/ALT elevations, no bilirubin elevation and no Hy's law cases; the data were shared with the FDA and other regulators, which did not ask for changes to monitoring protocols, and Vertex is confident in the safety profile based on the phase II data.
quarterly_data.figure: about 3,000 U.S. endocrinologists treating acromegaly; $5 billion peak sales potential

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Reshma Kewalramani said Vertex has been on a more than 10-year journey to diversify; CF remains foundational with more growth as ALYFTREK launches around the world and into lower age groups, and there is a last 5% of CF patients for whom Vertex does not yet have a therapy. With the Crinetics acquisition, rare endocrine (PALSONIFY, approved and launched in the U.S. and approved in Europe) has switched places with renal to become the fourth pillar, with renal following. In total Vertex has something like six programs in phase III and more than that in phase II.
quarterly_data.figure: last 5% of CF patients without a therapy; something like six programs in phase III

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Reshma Kewalramani sized IgA nephropathy at something like 300,000 patients between the U.S. and Europe, about 150,000 inside the U.S., plus another 1 million or so in Asia, calling it a common rare disease. Three APRIL or APRIL/BAFF medicines are launching within a year or so of each other; as a nephrologist she said a medicine acting on both APRIL and BAFF makes most sense for a B-cell-mediated disease, that on numerical cross-trial comparisons (to be taken with a grain of salt) povetacicept has the best proteinuria, hematuria and Gd-IgA1 response, and that its once-monthly small-volume auto-injector may be one of the greatest differentiators. Vertex has built the largest sales force to serve patients in community settings as well as centers of excellence.
quarterly_data.figure: about 300,000 IgAN patients in the U.S. and Europe, about 150,000 in the U.S., about 1 million in Asia

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Reshma Kewalramani said Vertex will not cut the povetacicept IgAN GFR dataset early: the FDA has all but said one-year GFR would be acceptable, but the MHRA, EMA, Asian regulators and Australia are not yet at the point where proteinuria is acceptable and accept two-year GFR, and Vertex's ambition is to launch povetacicept around the globe. On payers, Vertex has targeted and discussed povetacicept with more than 70% of payers since about last summer in productive and positive conversations, and she expects to secure reimbursement commensurate with what is already in the field. She expects the next povetacicept phase III readout to be in membranous nephropathy, with myasthenia gravis (in phase II) after that.
quarterly_data.figure: povetacicept discussed with more than 70% of payers

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Reshma Kewalramani said AMKD occurs only in people of recent Sub-Saharan African descent, with two APOL1 alleles raising the risk of progression something like 5x, 6x; there are about 100,000-150,000 people with AMKD in the United States and no medicines specifically approved for it. Unlike in IgAN, the FDA is not yet comfortable with proteinuria as the accelerated approval endpoint in AMKD, so AMPLITUDE's potential accelerated approval rests on one-year GFR; given the rapid decline in AMKD she is confident the study is powered correctly to show a difference at one year. After the AMPLIFY phase IIb data she expects to discuss next steps with regulators rather than move straight into more clinical trials, and suspects the agency would first want to see AMPLITUDE.
quarterly_data.figure: risk of progression something like 5x, 6x; about 100,000-150,000 people with AMKD in the U.S.

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Reshma Kewalramani said that for three, four years Vertex has offered free real-world genetic testing for AMKD with groups like Natera, alongside testing built into the phase III trial infrastructure, and has already identified a number of patients, giving a head start in patient identification if inaxaplin is approved.
quarterly_data.figure: free genetic testing programs running three, four years

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Reshma Kewalramani said the overlap between physicians who could use inaxaplin for AMKD and those who might use povetacicept for IgAN is about 70%, so the renal sales force can also bring out inaxaplin, followed by membranous nephropathy and ADPKD programs. On pricing she said the current wave of renal medicines' price points are a reasonable proxy for inaxaplin, since the health economics are very supportive.
quarterly_data.figure: about 70% prescriber overlap between inaxaplin and povetacicept

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Reshma Kewalramani said ALYFTREK is regulatorily approved in almost all regions, with pricing and access still being worked on in some; growth comes from switches from TRIKAFTA, naive patients with ultra-rare mutations (for example in Italy), lower age groups (two to five, then younger) and emerging countries such as Brazil and Turkiye that are still getting reimbursement. After Next Gen 3.0 (VX-828, VX-581, VX-272) there is a Next Gen 4.0 and she expects 5.0 and beyond; Vertex believes it has already reached the asymptote for ppFEV1 and is getting awful close on sweat chloride, where the carrier median is about 30 mmol, with abstracts submitted to the fall North American CF meeting. Ex-U.S. contracts are rebid every three, four years on real-world lung-function data, and Vertex has been able to hold price steady in some countries, though not in all.
quarterly_data.figure: ALYFTREK approved in almost all regions; sweat chloride carrier median about 30 mmol; ex-U.S. rebids every three, four years

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Reshma Kewalramani said atumelnant, from the Crinetics acquisition, has multi-billion dollar potential and the opportunity to serve some number between 15,000 and 20,000 congenital adrenal hyperplasia patients in the U.S. plus another 15,000 ex-U.S., as well as Cushing's disease; it is in phase III for CAH and phase I/II for Cushing's. In early-stage pipeline, the NaV1.7/1.8 combination is in late preclinical development with chemical matter in hand, now going through the standard procedures to reach the clinic.

quarterly_data.signal: Vertex's July 6, 2026 Crinetics acquisition investor presentation (Exhibit 99.1) describes PALSONIFY (paltusotine) as the first and only once-daily oral therapy for adults with acromegaly (company claim), FDA and EMA approved, with a U.S. launch in October 2025 and strong early uptake. It cites PATHFNDR-1 (switch patients from injected depot SRLs) and PATHFNDR-2 (naive/untreated patients), with patients with IGF-1 <=1x ULN as primary endpoint, 2-4 weeks to IGF-1 normalization in most patients, no serious AEs and improvement on patient-reported outcomes. Based on Q1:26 data PALSONIFY has ~40-50% new to brand Rx share, is on track to achieve 75% reimbursement coverage by Q3:26, and has ~80% endo unaided awareness with ~70% of endos saying they have a high intent to prescribe. The deck sizes acromegaly at ~20,000 diagnosed patients in the U.S. and another 35,000+ outside the U.S., and says only 18% of patients remain on injectable SRLs at ~3 years.
quarterly_data.figure: U.S. launch October 2025; ~40-50% new to brand Rx share (Q1:26); 75% reimbursement coverage targeted by Q3:26; ~20,000 U.S. and 35,000+ ex-U.S. acromegaly patients

quarterly_data.signal: The same presentation says atumelnant, a once-daily oral ACTH receptor antagonist, is in Phase 3 for adults and Phase 2/3 for pediatric patients with congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH), and that in Phase 2 it drove robust A4 reduction, sustained even with glucocorticoids reduced to physiologic levels. In ACTH-dependent Cushing's syndrome (ADCS) atumelnant Phase 1/2 data show rapid lowering of urine free cortisol (UFC), plus early indications of potential improvement in symptoms of hypercortisolism, and it was well tolerated. Vertex sizes classic CAH at ~17,000 diagnosed U.S. patients (~12,000 adults / ~5,000 pediatrics) plus 15,000+ outside the U.S., and ADCS at >10,000 U.S. patients plus ~15,000 outside the U.S.
quarterly_data.figure: CAH: Phase 3 adults, Phase 2/3 pediatric; ~17,000 U.S. classic CAH patients plus 15,000+ ex-U.S.; ADCS >10,000 U.S. plus ~15,000 ex-U.S.

quarterly_data.signal: Vertex describes Crinetics as ~600 employees, founded 2008 and headquartered in San Diego, with a GPCR drug discovery platform, IP protection into the 2040s and additional pre-clinical pipeline assets with potential in thyroid eye disease, Graves' disease and hyperparathyroidism. Vertex says its 2023 goal of "5 launches in 5 years" is achieved early with the Crinetics acquisition, which adds endocrine as a fifth pillar.

quarterly_data.signal: Vertex presented Phase 3 data at the European Cystic Fibrosis Conference for ALYFTREK in children 2 to 5 years of age: 65% of children, including those with F/F and F/MF genotypes, reached carrier sweat chloride levels of <30 mmol/L, with a mean reduction in sweat chloride of 9.6 mmol/L from a baseline on TRIKAFTA; ALYFTREK was generally safe and well tolerated. With the U.S. FDA approval in children 2 years of age and older with SCD or TDT, approximately 5,500 patients may be eligible for treatment with CASGEVY for the first time. In May Vertex secured reimbursement for CASGEVY for eligible patients 12 years and older with SCD or TDT in Germany, and it continues to advance preclinical assets for gentler conditioning toward clinical trials, which could broaden the eligible patient population.
quarterly_data.figure: approved in 39 countries; approximately 5,500 newly eligible U.S. patients ages 2+

quarterly_data.signal: During the second quarter Health Canada accepted Vertex's new drug submission for suzetrigine for moderate-to-severe acute pain, and review is underway. Twenty-three states provide coverage for JOURNAVX via Medicaid. In neuropathic pain, Vertex is on track to complete enrollment in a Phase 2 study of VX-993 in people with diabetic peripheral neuropathy by the end of 2026, and continues to advance toward clinical trials preclinical assets that inhibit NaV1.7 for use alone or in combination with a NaV1.8 inhibitor.
quarterly_data.figure: Health Canada review of suzetrigine underway; Twenty-three states provide Medicaid coverage; VX-993 Phase 2 DPN enrollment on track to complete by end of 2026

quarterly_data.signal: The povetacicept BLA for accelerated approval in adults with IgAN (PDUFA November 30, 2026) is supported by positive data from a pre-specified Week 36 interim analysis of the ongoing Phase 3 RAINIER trial; if approved, povetacicept will become the first commercialized therapy in Vertex's nephrology pillar. AGLOW, the VX-407 ADPKD study, is a 26-patient, single-arm, 52-week Phase 2 proof-of-concept study evaluating height-adjusted total kidney volume (htTKV) in patients with a subset of PKD1 variants estimated at up to approximately 30,000 (or up to approximately 10%) of the overall ADPKD population.

quarterly_data.signal: Ahead of the AMPLIFY phase IIb readout of inaxaplin, CEO Reshma Kewalramani set the bar for the modest-proteinuria cohort: she hesitated to offer a bar but said anything in the 20%, 30% range would be positive and that double-digit proteinuria improvement would be a positive given the smaller dynamic range; she said that, if she remembered correctly, the lowest level of proteinuria improvement that later turned out to have value when the sponsor did the time to ESRD, dialysis or death trial was something like 14%, 15%. She said Vertex had not yet had its end-of-phase II meeting with the FDA because it did not yet have the phase II data.

quarterly_data.signal: The U.S. FDA approved two Ziihera (zanidatamab-hrii) regimens for the first-line treatment of adults with unresectable locally advanced or metastatic HER2-positive gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma (GEA): Ziihera plus Tevimbra (tislelizumab-jsgr) and fluoropyrimidine- and platinum-containing chemotherapy for HER2+ IHC 3+ and IHC 2+/ISH+ disease regardless of PD-L1 status, and Ziihera plus the same chemotherapy for HER2+ IHC 3+ disease. In the Phase 3 HERIZON-GEA-01 trial both Ziihera combinations reduced the risk of disease progression or death by 35% and extended median PFS to 12.4 months versus 8.1 months with trastuzumab plus chemotherapy; the tislelizumab triplet reduced the risk of death by 28%, with median OS of 26.4 months versus 19.2 months. The U.S. label carries boxed warnings for diarrhea and embryo-fetal toxicity. CMO Rob Iannone called Ziihera the first and only bispecific HER2-targeted antibody combined with a PD-1 inhibitor and chemotherapy approved for all HER2+ advanced GEA patients regardless of PD-L1 status (company claim). Approximately 20% of GEA patients have HER2+ disease.

quarterly_data.signal: Ziihera first-line GEA label safety data: with chemotherapy and tislelizumab, diarrhea was reported in 85% of 330 patients in clinical studies (Grade 3 24%, Grade 4 2.1%; fatal outcomes 1.5%), serious adverse reactions occurred in 59% of 294 HERIZON-GEA-01 patients, fatal adverse reactions in 2.4% and permanent discontinuation of Ziihera in 13%; with chemotherapy alone, diarrhea was reported in 81% of 395 patients in clinical studies (Grade 3 20%, Grade 4 1.3%), serious adverse reactions occurred in 49% of 305 patients and permanent discontinuation in 10%. LVEF decrease was observed in 9% (with tislelizumab) and 5% (chemotherapy only) of patients.
quarterly_data.figure: diarrhea 85% of 330 / 81% of 395 patients; serious adverse reactions 59% / 49%; discontinuation 13% / 10%; LVEF decrease 9% / 5%

quarterly_data.quarter: Jazz Pharmaceuticals press release: Ziihera (zanidatamab-hrii) plus Chemotherapy Demonstrates (08-31-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Jazz announced second interim top-line overall survival (OS) results from the Phase 3 HERIZON-GEA-01 trial: Ziihera (zanidatamab-hrii) plus chemotherapy demonstrated statistically significant and clinically meaningful OS improvement versus trastuzumab plus chemotherapy in first-line HER2+ locally advanced or metastatic GEA, and with longer follow-up the OS hazard ratios of both the Ziihera plus chemotherapy arm and the Ziihera plus Tevimbra (tislelizumab-jsgr) and chemotherapy arm improved compared with the first interim analysis. The safety profile was generally consistent with the known profile of each agent, with no new safety signals observed. Jazz has submitted the data for presentation at a major medical meeting in the fourth quarter 2026 and will also submit them to global health authorities. The global, randomized, open-label trial, run jointly with BeOne Medicines, randomized 914 patients from approximately 225 sites in more than 30 countries, with dual primary endpoints of PFS per BICR and OS.
quarterly_data.figure: Ziihera plus chemotherapy OS statistically significant at second interim analysis; OS hazard ratios of both Ziihera arms improved vs first interim; data submitted for presentation at a major medical meeting in fourth quarter 2026; 914 patients, approximately 225 sites, more than 30 countries

quarterly_data.quarter: Jazz Pharmaceuticals press release: Jazz Pharmaceuticals Completes Acquisition of Actio (09-15-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Jazz completed its acquisition of Actio Biosciences on September 15, 2026; Actio is now a wholly-owned subsidiary. The release adds ABS-1230 study detail: in preclinical studies, ABS-1230, an orally available small molecule KCNT1 inhibitor, inhibited KCNT1 across all evaluable pathogenic mutations, which the company says indicates potential to treat all patients with KCNT1-related epilepsy; CEO Renee Gala called it a potential 'transformative, first-in-class therapy' (company claim).
quarterly_data.figure: acquisition completed September 15, 2026; preclinical KCNT1 inhibition across all evaluable pathogenic mutations

quarterly_data.quarter: Jazz Pharmaceuticals Deutsche Bank Healthcare Summit 2026 (09-16-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Chief R&D Officer Rob on zanidatamab clinical data: the biliary tract cancer data showed an 'over 40% response rate, very durable'; Jazz's phase II in frontline gastric cancer showed activity in PD-L1 negative patients, although four prior studies with three different PD-1 antibodies had shown no activity in PD-L1 low patients; at the first interim analysis of HERIZON-GEA-01 the triplet arm had a statistically significant OS benefit, with two additional scheduled OS analyses. The frontline BTC pivotal trial is enrolling against no approved HER2 therapy, with probably 80% of patients globally expected to get a PD-1 or PD-L1 inhibitor in combination, and he said the trial 'is going to be successful to enroll on the timelines that we are planning for.' Colorectal cancer activity seen in the pan-tumor trial has not yet been published.
quarterly_data.figure: BTC response rate over 40%; probably 80% of frontline BTC patients globally on a PD-1 or PD-L1 inhibitor combination

quarterly_data.quarter: Jazz Pharmaceuticals Deutsche Bank Healthcare Summit 2026 (09-16-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Chief R&D Officer Rob on other clinical evidence: the IMforte trial of Zepzelca maintenance in small cell lung cancer was published in The Lancet; for Epidiolex (currently indicated for seizures associated with three DEEs - Dravet, TSC and LGS) Jazz has published caregiver surveys showing perceived benefits on behavior and cognition and recently published the EpiCom study of behavior and cognition in TSC patients; he called Epidiolex the largest grossing epilepsy drug (company claim). The next-generation orexin 2 agonist program targets a shorter half-life and good brain penetrance, and Jazz expects healthy volunteer data in the near future. On Actio's KCNT1 inhibitor he said KCNT1 is a gain-of-function single-gene driver, that experimentally knocking the channel down gave a benign phenotype with very little toxicity (taking the gene out entirely in mice showed no problems), and that clinical data seen in due diligence are not yet public.
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure

quarterly_data.signal: On the post-Enhertu breast cancer phase III, CMO Rob Iannone said 'we have data showing that zanidatamab, given its unique mechanism of action, is active even in patients who've progressed on Enhertu,' coming from monotherapy data, from combination data with standard of care in the HER2-positive, ER-positive population that Jazz published, and from combinations with novel agents like the ALX agent. He said zanidatamab would, he thinks, be unique in having data demonstrating its activity versus standard of care in patients who've progressed on Enhertu, regardless of the line of therapy.
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure

players.product: precision-oncology companion diagnostic programs

quarterly_data.signal: The phase III CLARITY-Gastric01 trial of sonesitatug vedotin demonstrated an overall survival benefit in patients with CLDN18.2 expression as low as 25% at any staining intensity, a lower threshold than that required by other CLDN18.2 targeted therapies. Dave Fredrickson said the company expanded the definition of CLDN18.2 positivity with a cutoff of greater than 25%, which represents about half of patients with gastric GEJ cancer, or more than 180,000 patients across the U.S., EU5, China and Japan. Management estimated peak year revenue of $3 billion-$5 billion for the ADC.
quarterly_data.figure: CLDN18.2 cutoff >25%; ~50% of 2L+ gastric patients; >180,000 patients; peak revenue $3B-$5B

quarterly_data.signal: Biomarker testing infrastructure was flagged as a commercial gating factor. For Truqap in PTEN-deficient metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer following the CAPItello-281 approval, management said 'a near-term priority is to establish testing in the setting, which today is not common practice.' Truqap revenue was $233 million in the quarter, up 37%. In the AVANZAR trial both the intention-to-treat and the TROP2 biomarker-positive populations sit at the top of the multiple testing procedure, so a positive study can come from either group. For Ultomiris in HSCT-TMA, discussions with health authorities are ongoing on interpreting the data 'including in the context of real-world evidence.'
quarterly_data.figure: Truqap revenue $233M (+37%)

quarterly_data.signal: Core R&D expense increased 6% in the first half and represented 23% of total revenue; management expects full-year R&D at the upper end of the low 20s percentage range as it builds out bispecifics, cell therapies and T-cell engagers. Capital expenditure was $1.5 billion in the first half and is expected to increase by around a third in 2026, including a new ADC manufacturing facility in Singapore, and the company opened a new Kendall Square R&D center in Cambridge. Deal-related payments totaled $3.3 billion and new BD transactions totaled just over $2 billion in upfront payments year to date.
quarterly_data.figure: core R&D +6%, 23% of revenue; H1 capex $1.5B, +~1/3 in 2026; deal payments $3.3B; BD upfronts >$2B YTD

quarterly_data.signal: Six high-value phase III programs read out positively in the first half, including first pivotal data for three new molecular entities, and the company secured 30 major market approvals. Pascal Soriot said 25 key phase III trial readouts are planned over the next 18 months, with pivotal data readouts for six new molecular entities in 2027 alone. Saruparib in prostate cancer was singled out as a $5 billion-range opportunity reading out next year.
quarterly_data.figure: 25 phase III readouts in 18 months; 6 NME pivotal readouts in 2027; 30 major market approvals in H1

quarterly_data.signal: First-half total revenue grew 6%, or 11% excluding Farxiga and Brilinta which are affected by generics, and core EPS grew 11%. Oncology total revenue grew 15% to $14.1 billion with the U.S. up 18% and Europe up 16%; Rare Disease grew 11% to $4.9 billion; BioPharmaceuticals declined 5% to $11.2 billion on loss of exclusivity for Farxiga, Brilinta and roxadustat. Core gross margin was 83% in the first half.
quarterly_data.figure: total revenue +6% (+11% ex-Farxiga/Brilinta); core EPS +11%; oncology $14.1B (+15%); rare disease $4.9B (+11%); BioPharma $11.2B (-5%); core gross margin 83%

quarterly_data.signal: Full-year guidance was reiterated: total revenue to increase by a mid-to-high single-digit percentage and core EPS by a low double-digit percentage at constant exchange rates. Management reaffirmed the risk-adjusted $80 billion revenue ambition for 2030, noting 11 approved new molecular entities against a target of 20 by 2030, and said it does not need additional business development to deliver post-2030 growth.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue mid-to-high single digit; core EPS low double digit CER; $80B by 2030; 11 of 20 NMEs approved

quarterly_data.signal: Second-quarter regulatory output: Pascal Soriot said the company 'received eight major market approvals across important indications, including two additional NMEs.' These included the first approvals for Enhertu in first-line hormone receptor-positive breast cancer with emergent ESR1 mutations in Europe and Japan and a few other countries, with constructive discussions continuing with the U.S. FDA, and U.S. FDA approval for Baxfendy, 'which has the potential to transform outcomes for patients with uncontrolled or resistant hypertension.' For the first half he identified the two first NME approvals as camizestrant in breast cancer and Baxfendy in hypertension.
quarterly_data.figure: 8 major market approvals in Q2 including two additional NMEs

quarterly_data.signal: China: Pascal Soriot said growth 'was impacted by continued effects from volume-based procurement, and we expect the recent NRDL additions and new regulatory approval in 2026 to fuel future growth,' while the U.S., Europe and emerging markets outside of China grew strongly. Asked whether he was still confident on the country, he said he remains 'still very bullish for reasons that have evolved' - Chinese companies are innovating at great speed and tend to partner with global companies to globalize development and commercialization, competition in the Tagrisso market and the ADC market is very intense, and being strongly present in China let the Chinese team play a role in the speedy development of Sone-Ve.
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure

quarterly_data.signal: Core P&L detail below the top line. CFO Aradhana Sarin said product revenue grew 6% in the first half while alliance revenue increased by 29%, 'reflecting higher profit shares from our partnered medicines Enhertu, Datverzo, and Tezspire in markets where our partners record product sales.' Core gross margin of 83% improved in the second quarter compared to the first, but a lower second-half margin is expected 'consistent with prior years, reflecting seasonal demand patterns for lower-margin medicines such as FluMist and Beyfortus,' with full-year core gross margin stable to slightly higher versus 2025. Core SG&A expense also increased by 6% in the first half, covering the U.S. Baxfendy launch and pre-launch investment ahead of tozorakimab. Other operating income was $341 million in the first six months, consisting of royalties and small regional divestitures, with a broadly similar level anticipated in the second half; in Q&A she added there is a portion of it 'that is consistent and will likely continue into 2027.' Guidance for 2027 will be given at the beginning of 2027, after an annual budgeting process that starts later this year.
quarterly_data.figure: product revenue +6%; alliance revenue +29%; core gross margin 83% in H1; core SG&A +6%; other operating income $341M

quarterly_data.signal: Cash, working capital and capital structure. Aradhana Sarin reported '$1.2 billion in the first half, a decline versus comparator period' (the transcript drops the line-item label), which 'primarily reflects the Lynparza milestone received in the first quarter of 2025, skewing comparisons, as well as working capital impact associated with U.S. loss of exclusivity for Farxiga'; those working capital effects are expected to persist through the remainder of the year before normalizing. The second-quarter tax rate benefited from a one-time adjustment to deferred tax assets following certain internal legal entity changes. Deal-related payments included the $1.2 billion upfront payment for the CSPC collaboration, which closed during the second quarter, and the company continues to expect milestone payments of approximately $2.5 billion for the full year relating to prior business development transactions, with the most recently announced Dizal transaction included in the year-to-date BD upfronts. Net debt increased by around $3.5 billion in the first half, primarily reflecting the second FY 2025 interim dividend paid in March and those deal payments; the company remains comfortable with its level of gross debt, and core finance costs are expected to be higher in the second half following refinancing at higher than historic interest rates and lower interest income.
quarterly_data.figure: $1.2B in H1 (decline vs comparator period); CSPC upfront $1.2B; FY milestone payments ~$2.5B; net debt +~$3.5B

quarterly_data.signal: EGFR-mutated lung franchise. Dave Fredrickson said Tagrisso delivered 6% growth in the second quarter to revenues of $1.9 billion, supported by double-digit growth in the U.S., and that it is the number one prescribed third-generation EGFR TKI globally, approved across all stages of disease; in the highly competitive U.S. market FLAURA2 holds around three-quarters of the growing first-line combination segment. Against the MARIPOSA regimen and intense Chinese competition he said 'we're seeing double-digit volume growth, and in fact, double-digit revenue growth in the U.S.' AstraZeneca also announced the in-licensing of Zegfrovy, a novel oral EGFR inhibitor already approved in the U.S. and China for tumors carrying exon 20 insertion mutations following progression on or after platinum-based chemotherapy; based on the WU-KONG28 data presented at ASCO, first-line filings have been submitted in China and the U.S. Susan Galbraith said the asset, licensed from Dizal, is also active in non-classical mutations, 'which is about a similar size patient population.'
quarterly_data.figure: Tagrisso $1.9B (+6%); FLAURA2 ~three-quarters of the U.S. first-line combination segment

quarterly_data.signal: Calquence grew 16% in the quarter, 'generating more than $1 billion in revenue for the first time in a single quarter,' and Dave Fredrickson said it maintains its position as the leading BTK inhibitor in frontline CLL across major markets despite intense competition. Within the finite duration class, AMPLIFY continues to gain share in reimbursed markets with encouraging early signs in the U.S., where it is uniquely positioned as the only BTK inhibitor with both finite and treat-to-progression options; management sees AMPLIFY as a significant growth driver through the remainder of 2026, supported by the clear global trend towards adoption of finite duration treatments.
quarterly_data.figure: Calquence +16%; more than $1 billion in a single quarter for the first time

quarterly_data.signal: Imfinzi and Imjudo delivered growth of 25% in aggregate in the second quarter, with meaningful contributions from MATTERHORN in gastric cancer and ADRIATIC in lung. Susan Galbraith reported that the phase III VOLGA interim analysis in muscle-invasive bladder cancer, covering 'the 50% of patients who are not candidates for cisplatin,' showed Imfinzi in combination with enfortumab vedotin delivering statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvements in both event-free survival and overall survival, while the Imjudo-containing arm showed a statistically significant improvement in event-free survival with a favorable trend in overall survival. Positive NILE results also came this quarter, and VOLGA complements NIAGARA and the recently U.S.-approved POTOMAC indication in earlier-stage non-muscle-invasive disease.
quarterly_data.figure: Imfinzi and Imjudo +25% aggregate in Q2; VOLGA addresses the 50% of patients not candidates for cisplatin

quarterly_data.signal: Enhertu grew 31% in the quarter to reported revenues of $888 million, with growth across all regions reflecting sustained market leadership in the HER2-positive and HER2-low breast cancer indications in major markets plus increased adoption and additional launches in emerging markets. Dave Fredrickson cited encouraging early signs of adoption and growing awareness in the first-line DESTINY-Breast09 setting in the United States following its approval late last year, and said the recent simultaneous U.S. approvals of DESTINY-Breast05 and DESTINY-Breast11 in the curative setting will become increasingly important through the remainder of the year.
quarterly_data.figure: Enhertu $888M (+31%)

quarterly_data.signal: Datroway revenues of $55 million in the second quarter showed growing demand in later-line EGFR-mutated lung cancer with increasing second-line utilization in the U.S., and the launch in triple-negative breast cancer for patients who are not candidates for immunotherapy is underway following the U.S. approval of TROPION-Breast02 earlier in the quarter. Susan Galbraith argued AstraZeneca has 'a best-in-class TROP2-based ADC based on the design, which is based on the stable linker,' pointing to the half-life of the molecule and a lower rate of bone marrow toxicity than ADCs with less stable linkers and more exposure to the free payload. Two phase III trials read out later this year in the post-TKI second-line setting - TROPION-Lung15 (Datroway alone and in combination with Tagrisso) and SAFFRON (Tagrisso combined with Orpathys in MET-driven resistance) - while TROPION-Lung14 aims to bring the Datroway plus Tagrisso combination into the first line.
quarterly_data.figure: Datroway $55M in Q2

quarterly_data.signal: CLARITY-Gastric01 trial detail and the wholly-owned ADC franchise. Susan Galbraith said the trial met its overall survival dual primary endpoint with a statistically significant and highly clinically meaningful improvement versus investigator's choice of therapy in patients treated with at least two prior therapies, that there was a trend to PFS benefit which did not meet statistical significance, and that the key secondary endpoint also showed a highly clinically meaningful overall survival benefit in patients treated with at least one prior line. 'Fewer than 20% of patients with advanced gastric cancer survive beyond one year.' Sone-Ve is the first phase III data from the wholly-owned ADC portfolio, the second AstraZeneca ADC to demonstrate an overall survival benefit in gastric cancer after Enhertu, and the third positive phase III readout in this tumor type in just two years following MATTERHORN and DESTINY-Gastric04. The first-line CLARITY-Gastric02 study has a PD-L1 greater than 1% cohort and a less than 1% cohort, combining Sone-Ve with capecitabine with or without Rilvegostomig or nivolumab, and CLDN18.2 is also expressed on some pancreatic and biliary tract cancers being explored in ongoing phase I.
quarterly_data.figure: fewer than 20% of patients with advanced gastric cancer survive beyond one year

quarterly_data.signal: Breast and prostate phase III design detail. On camizestrant, Susan Galbraith said SERENA-4 has 'a larger sample size, 1,370 patients enrolled compared to PERSEVERE,' is designed to enrich for endocrine sensitivity, and is anticipated to read out in the second half of this year; she described an overall tolerability profile with low rates of GI side effects and a very low discontinuation rate. CAMBRIA-1 is an extended adjuvant switch trial in intermediate-to-high-risk hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative patients who have completed two-five years of adjuvant endocrine therapy with or without a CDK4/6 inhibitor, which she said selects for an endocrine-sensitive population and 'has a good probability of success.' For saruparib, EvoPAR-Prostate01 is in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer and is powered for both the HRRM and non-HRRM cohorts, taking the learnings from PROpel into an earlier line, with the EvoPAR-Breast opportunity alongside it.
quarterly_data.figure: SERENA-4: 1,370 patients enrolled, readout in the second half of this year; CAMBRIA-1 enrolls patients who completed two-five years of adjuvant endocrine therapy

quarterly_data.signal: BioPharmaceuticals second-quarter product performance. Ruud Dobber said respiratory and immunology total revenue grew by 11%, with the established biologics for severe asthma generating 'over $2 billion of in-market sales in the first half.' Fasenra grew 13% to $570 million on continued IL-5 class leadership and grew 75% in emerging markets thanks to its launch in China, where it entered the National Reimbursement Drug List at the start of the year. Tezspire grew by 45% to $390 million. Breztri grew 20% to $346 million, received its first approval for asthma this year in the United States and a positive CHMP recommendation for asthma in Europe last week. Symbicort revenues of $671 million were down 8% on U.S. price pressure from a new generic competitor entering the market. Saphnelo increased 24% to $209 million on share gains in the intravenous segment for SLE patients, with a new subcutaneous formulation now available in the U.S. and some European markets.
quarterly_data.figure: R&I revenue +11%; severe asthma biologics >$2B in-market H1; Fasenra $570M (+13%, EM +75%); Tezspire $390M (+45%); Breztri $346M (+20%); Symbicort $671M (-8%); Saphnelo $209M (+24%)

quarterly_data.signal: Farxiga loss of exclusivity and its lifecycle defense. Ruud Dobber said generic competition entered the U.S. at the start of the quarter and that this, along with loss of exclusivity in some other markets and VBP in China, 'saw Farxiga decline by 90% overall, resulting in $1.8 billion of revenue for the quarter.' Three fixed-dose combinations are in development: Zibo-Depa, in phase III and recruiting very fast in proteinuria CKD; Balci-Depa in heart failure patients with a low eGFR where mortality is normally twice that of a normal heart failure patient and where 'more than 12 million patients in the top eight markets are eligible for a treatment like this'; and baxdrostat in combination with dapagliflozin in chronic kidney disease and hypertension. Data for both fixed-dose combinations are expected in the first half of 2027, building on dapagliflozin, of which Dobber said '60 million patients are currently treated.'
quarterly_data.figure: Farxiga -90% to $1.8B revenue for the quarter; >12 million eligible patients in the top eight markets; 60 million patients currently treated with dapagliflozin; FDC data in H1 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Baxfendy launch and the primary aldosteronism opportunity. Ruud Dobber said the U.S. approval and launch were secured in May and the company is building early market access through affordability programs, with commercial access expected to broaden over the next few quarters 'in anticipation of Medicare Part D reimbursements from 2028.' Sharon Barr said primary aldosteronism is the leading cause of secondary hypertension and 'could affect as many as 5%-10% of all hypertensives and up to 20% of resistant hypertension,' that relatively few of those patients are screened today because there has been no therapy to give them, and that AstraZeneca has 'the first approved aldosterone synthase inhibitor'; the primary aldosteronism study has accrued very rapidly and the company is accelerating that timeline.
quarterly_data.figure: primary aldosteronism could affect as many as 5%-10% of all hypertensives and up to 20% of resistant hypertension; Medicare Part D reimbursement from 2028

quarterly_data.signal: Respiratory pipeline. Sharon Barr said the highly clinically meaningful OBERON and TITANIA phase III results for tozorakimab in COPD will be presented at the European Respiratory Society Congress in September, describing a potential first and best-in-class asset, and Pascal Soriot said that as a result 'we have increased our peak revenue expectation to more than $5 billion' for a product very few people thought would work and to which AstraZeneca itself had assigned a low probability of success. Ruud Dobber attributed the result to a mechanism 'inhibiting the anti-inflammatory pathway, but equally the mucus pathway,' and said the company is 'making an early start on our launch preparations for tezepelumab' (as spoken while describing the OBERON and TITANIA COPD data). Elsewhere in respiratory, the inhaled TSLP Sunakiment, formerly referred to as AZD8630, read out its phase II study with phase III plans under discussion with partner Amgen, and AstraZeneca entered an exclusive license agreement with CTTQ, a subsidiary of Sino Biopharmaceutical, for the development, manufacturing and commercialization of TQC3721, an inhaled small molecule PDE3/4 inhibitor already in phase III trials in China for COPD.
quarterly_data.figure: tozorakimab peak revenue expectation increased to more than $5 billion

quarterly_data.signal: The CARDIO-TTRansform miss and how it unwinds against the 2026 readout cohort. Sharon Barr said that in a contemporary ATTR cardiomyopathy population treated with standard of care, 'including 57% on a stabilizer,' adding Wainua did not provide a statistically significant benefit on the composite outcome of CV mortality and recurrent CV events; a pre-specified subgroup of patients on Wainua monotherapy showed fewer primary composite events, a nominally significant result, while no treatment effect was observed in patients on stabilizer therapy at baseline. AstraZeneca and Ionis will analyze the full data set and present at the European Society of Cardiology Congress in August. Aradhana Sarin said the $10 billion figure was 'the peak year estimates with the risk unwind' for the 2026 cohort, that some have unwound in a positive manner like Tozo and some not so positively like Wainua, and that 'I still think we'll unwind close to $10 billion' - not a 2030 number, since peak for some of these products may hit beyond 2030. Pascal Soriot added that AstraZeneca owns tozorakimab 100% whereas Wainua was to be shared with partner Ionis, so 'we gained more with Tozo than we lost with Wainua.'
quarterly_data.figure: 57% on a stabilizer in CARDIO-TTRansform; 2026 cohort still expected to unwind close to $10 billion in peak year sales

quarterly_data.signal: Cardiometabolic pipeline. Sharon Barr said the phase II-B VISTA trial of the oral GLP-1 elecoglipron showed 'a clinically meaningful and statistically significant weight loss of up to 11.8% at week 36, importantly, without evidence of a plateau,' while SOLSTICE showed 'an up to 1.9% reduction in HbA1c at week 26,' with a favorable safety profile and low discontinuation rates. First subject in was achieved for both EMBOLD (monotherapy in obesity or overweight) and ILLUMINATE (five phase III trials in Type 2 diabetes, as monotherapy and in combination with dapagliflozin), and ELEVATE is planned in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and chronic kidney disease; Pascal Soriot said 'we have now initiated five phase III trials for elecoglipron.' Beyond GLP-1, the phase II APRICUS trial of the selective amylin receptor agonist AZD6234 read out this quarter with a phase III monotherapy trial now initiating and data to be shared at EASD; the oral PCSK9 lariprostat has a phase III readout in the first half of 2027 with a first fixed-dose combination of lariprostat with rosuvastatin advancing into phase III, and Soriot said a further fixed-dose combination with elecoglipron is being developed. Ruud Dobber said the competitor's official first U.S. list price 'will not change dramatically our own outlook.'
quarterly_data.figure: VISTA weight loss up to 11.8% at week 36; SOLSTICE up to 1.9% HbA1c reduction at week 26; five phase III trials initiated for elecoglipron; oral PCSK9 phase III readout in H1 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Rare Disease medicine-level performance. Marc Dunoyer said second-quarter Ultomiris grew 12% on patient demand across indications including the competitive MG and PNH markets, while Soliris revenues continued to decline due to successful conversion to Ultomiris as well as biosimilar pressure. Strensiq grew 36% year-on-year and 'remains one of AstraZeneca's fastest-growing blockbuster medicines,' supported by ongoing investment in commercial capabilities, infrastructure and disease awareness that also lays the foundation for the potential launch of efzimfotase alfa. Vosoritide continued to deliver strong global momentum, supported by expansion in adult patients with NF1-PN and uptake of the granule formulation in recently launched markets, and remained the market leader for pediatric patients with NF1-PN.
quarterly_data.figure: Ultomiris +12%; Strensiq +36%

quarterly_data.signal: Complement franchise pipeline. Marc Dunoyer said phase III I CAN data for Ultomiris in IgA nephropathy showed 'a 43% reduction in proteinuria, with significant proteinuria reduction seen as early as 10 weeks,' consistent across patient groups including those at higher risk of progression, and the company has now filed in both the U.S. and Japan. In HSCT-TMA, Ultomiris 'did not achieve statistical significance for the primary endpoint of event-free survival through 26 weeks compared to placebo in adults and adolescents aged 12 years older,' though it showed a trend towards treatment benefit; in pediatric patients AstraZeneca is advancing regulatory filings based on the open-label phase III trial reported in 2025 and data from an external control study. Asked about longer-acting C5 competitors, Dunoyer said the franchise continues to grow and the response is to pioneer new indications - IgAN, HSCT-TMA, delayed graft function and other renal rare diseases - and to develop other nodes of complement biology beyond C5.
quarterly_data.figure: I CAN: 43% reduction in proteinuria, significant reduction as early as 10 weeks; HSCT-TMA primary endpoint of event-free survival through 26 weeks not met

quarterly_data.signal: efzimfotase alfa in hypophosphatasia. Marc Dunoyer said the phase III pediatric MULBERRY and CHESTNUT data were presented at the International Conference on Children's Bone Health in June, and that in a pooled analysis of the phase III MULBERRY and HICKORY trials including pediatric, adolescent and adult patients, treatment 'resulted in a median of 361 days per year free from injection site reactions,' with injection site reaction rates 'five times lower than with Strensiq'; HICKORY data will be presented at the American Society for Bone and Mineral Research in October. In Q&A he said the filings 'will be above two years of age for a broad population,' done in discussion with regulatory authorities, covering adults with pediatric onset (already obtained in several countries with Strensiq) and adults with adult onset (where Strensiq is not approved today), and that 'even if we get less than the totality of the label that we have filed for, we expect to be within the range of $3 billion-$5 billion.' He contrasted dosing every two weeks against daily or every-other-day Strensiq and said patients on efzimfotase alfa have 'five days of injection site reaction on average in a given year,' which should improve country coverage, label breadth and patient retention.
quarterly_data.figure: median of 361 days per year free from injection site reactions; ISR rates five times lower than Strensiq; five days of ISR on average per year; filings above two years of age; peak sales within $3 billion-$5 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Other Rare Disease programs. Marc Dunoyer said phase III CALYPSO data presented in May at ECE showed eneboparatide maintaining serum calcium within the target range, normalizing urinary calcium and restoring normal bone turnover in patients with hypoparathyroidism. For anselamimab in kappa light chain amyloidosis, results from the CARES program 'demonstrated a 62% reduction in all-cause mortality and a 71% reduction in cardiovascular hospitalization,' with an overall survival benefit observed even in patients with advanced Mayo stage disease. On the TTR depleter cliramitug, he said the trial is run 'as an add-on to either stabilizer, tafamidis or acoramidis, and Silences' and not as a monotherapy, that depletion of amyloid burden in the tissues was confirmed during phase I-B studies over one year, and that anselamimab provides a read-across for the depleter mechanism in amyloidosis; Pascal Soriot added that cliramitug can be used as monotherapy, on top of vutrisiran, or on top of stabilizers.

quarterly_data.signal: Post-2030 growth platforms and the probability-of-success assumption behind the plan. Pascal Soriot said three recent launches - Datverzo, Etcamah and Baxfendy - each carry 'peak year revenue potential of more than $5 billion.' In next-generation IO, 'we now have 16 phase III trials across eight tumor types, including five in combination with our ADCs,' supporting an ambition to replace the current generation of checkpoint inhibitors. AZD0120 and surovatamig each have multiple phase III trials underway across hematology and both have now extended into autoimmune diseases, alongside investment in off-the-shelf and in vivo cell therapies. quarterly_data.quarter: AstraZeneca press release: Etcamah in combination with a CDK4/6 inhibitor approved in (09-04-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: The US FDA granted accelerated approval to Etcamah (camizestrant), a once-daily oral next-generation SERD, in combination with a CDK4/6 inhibitor (abemaciclib, palbociclib or ribociclib) for adults with HR-positive, HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer upon detection of an ESR1 mutation during aromatase inhibitor (AI) and CDK4/6 inhibitor therapy, based on an FDA-authorised test; concurrently the FDA approved a companion diagnostic test that detects emerging ESR1 mutations in circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA). The approval rests on the SERENA-6 Phase III trial (315 patients): the combination reduced the risk of disease progression or death by 56% versus an AI plus a CDK4/6 inhibitor (HR 0.44; median PFS 16.0 versus 9.2 months), a later pre-planned analysis showed a PFS2 benefit of 25.7 versus 19.1 months (HR 0.63), and overall survival is still maturing. The company cites approximately 37,000 US patients with HR-positive metastatic breast cancer treated with a medicine in the 1st-line setting, approximately 30% of whom develop ESR1 mutations during 1st-line treatment before progression. Etcamah is also approved in more than 30 countries, including the EU, Japan, Canada and the UK.

Bayer is open to deals with Chinese biotech, having done partnerships with Chinese biotech companies and startups.
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Bill Anderson on litigation: on June 25th the U.S. Supreme Court ruled in Monsanto v. Durnell that claims grounded in state failure-to-warn theories are preempted, which he called 'a really important step for limiting litigation in the future.' The proposed class settlement is moving ahead; the opt-out period closed on June 4th and the final approval hearing in Missouri state court is scheduled for August 19th, with a final decision expected later this year. On PCBs, Bayer aims to enforce Monsanto's indemnity agreements, with a case moving forward in federal court.
quarterly_data.figure: class settlement final approval hearing August 19th; opt-out period closed June 4th

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Bill Anderson: headcount in Q2 was roughly stable with no fixed job-reduction target under Dynamic Shared Ownership; AI is being incorporated very rapidly in enterprise systems and tools for staff, and he expects Bayer to get leaner and more productive over time. On structure, management keeps an open mind on spin-offs or divestitures but will stay focused on five priorities: the pharma pipeline, containing litigation, de-leveraging, Crop Science profitability and a leaner company. Low water on the Rhine has so far had no impact on Bayer.
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure

quarterly_data.signal: Management on European drug pricing: CFO Judith Hartmann said that in the time since AMNOG was formed, prices for pharmaceuticals in Germany have gone down about 10% while consumer prices increased 30% or 40%, calling this unsustainable and a threat to future innovation. CEO Bill Anderson said Bayer was disappointed by Germany's recent healthcare reform increasing the discounts and mandatory rebates from pharmaceutical companies and urged the government to reconsider, noting that about 80% of the medicines consumed in Germany are produced in Germany; he said Bayer has heard from the German government that it remains very committed to the long-term funding of pharmaceuticals but there is a need to balance the budget this year, with conversations between industry representatives and the government ongoing.
quarterly_data.figure: German pharma prices down about 10% since AMNOG vs consumer prices up 30% or 40%; about 80% of medicines consumed in Germany produced in Germany

players.product: automated biological discovery programs

quarterly_data.signal: Management leaned on real-world and third-party data to evidence the Wegovy pill launch: 'a recently published study showed that weight loss in the real world exceeded that seen in the OASIS 4 clinical trial at the same point in time.' The U.K. launch was tracked using IQVIA sell-in data to private providers and pharmacies, which showed Novo Nordisk obesity market share rising from around 30% before launch to 45% in July, with around 300,000 patients started in three weeks. Novo now serves more than 46 million people living with obesity and diabetes, with around 1.5 million people on the Wegovy pill worldwide and over 5 million total prescriptions.
quarterly_data.figure: obesity share ~30% to 45% (IQVIA July sell-in); ~300,000 U.K. patients in 3 weeks; 46M people served; 1.5M on Wegovy pill; >5M total prescriptions

quarterly_data.signal: The ZEUS cardiovascular outcomes trial of ziltivekimab, with more than 6,300 people enrolled, failed to reduce MACE with a hazard ratio of 0.99 despite confirmed target engagement and reductions in free IL-6 and hsCRP. Martin Holst Lange framed it as a biomarker-causality test: 'There was a question on the correlation between the biomarkers and the actual outcomes, and that was the leap of faith that had to be tested.' For zenagamtide, an extra titration step was added and management said that 'from a modeling perspective, feel quite confident that we'll see a safety tolerability profile in line with what we've seen with, for example, CagriSema.'
quarterly_data.figure: ZEUS >6,300 patients; MACE hazard ratio 0.99; all-cause mortality hazard ratio 0.99

quarterly_data.signal: Novo invested more than DKK 26 billion into R&D and commercial activities in the quarter, received more than 10 regulatory approvals and started more than 5 clinical trials. The company-wide transformation is running ahead of plan on DKK 8 billion of savings, which are being reinvested into growth opportunities; full-time employees fell to around 66,700, a decrease of almost 12,000 or roughly 15% versus 12 months ago.
quarterly_data.figure: DKK 26B R&D and commercial investment; >10 approvals; >5 trials started; DKK 8B savings; ~66,700 FTEs (-12,000, -15%)

quarterly_data.signal: Second-quarter adjusted sales increased 7% at constant exchange rates to DKK 78.5 billion, driven by GLP-1 volume growth and a favorable prior-period rebate adjustment. Obesity care sales rose 16% and GLP-1 diabetes sales rose 2%; U.S. Operations grew 4% and International Operations grew 10%. Adjusted operating profit increased 11% at constant exchange rates, while adjusted gross margin was 78.2% versus 82.7% a year earlier, including a one-time cost of around DKK 3 billion for right sizing manufacturing capacity agreements.
quarterly_data.figure: adjusted sales DKK 78.5B (+7% CER); obesity +16%; GLP-1 diabetes +2%; U.S. +4%; IO +10%; operating profit +11% CER; gross margin 78.2% vs 82.7%

quarterly_data.signal: Full-year 2026 guidance was raised again: adjusted sales growth is now expected at 0% to -6% at constant exchange rates and adjusted operating profit growth at 0% to -6%, driven mainly by increased expectations for GLP-1 product sales. The outlook assumes growth in International Operations and decline in U.S. Operations, semaglutide compound patent expiry in certain markets, reduced Medicaid obesity coverage and lower realized prices amplified by most favored nation agreements with the U.S. administration.
quarterly_data.figure: adjusted sales growth 0% to -6% CER; adjusted operating profit growth 0% to -6% CER

quarterly_data.signal: Management still expects a U.S. regulatory decision for CagriSema in obesity at the end of 2026 with a potential launch in 2027, and a U.S. regulatory decision for oral semaglutide 25 mg in type 2 diabetes plus U.S. and EU decisions for denecimig in hemophilia A. The ARTEMIS and HERMES cardiovascular outcomes trials of ziltivekimab continue with results expected in the first half of 2027, etavopivat is on track for EU and U.S. submission in Q4 2026, and the company will hold a Capital Markets Day in September.
