quarterly_data.signal: CEO Mike Doustdar sized the treated patient base: Novo Nordisk is 'treating almost 70% more people living with obesity compared to just a year ago, with nearly 5 million people on our obesity treatments.' He framed the quarter around three priorities - improve commercial competitiveness, progress the pipeline, and make focused investments while delivering returns.
quarterly_data.figure: almost 70% more people on obesity treatment year over year; nearly 5 million people on obesity treatments

quarterly_data.signal: U.S. Operations EVP Jamey Millar quantified the Wegovy pill launch six months in: it is 'the strongest-ever GLP-1 launch by volume.' It took 12 weeks to reach the first 1 million TRx, while the latest 1 million TRx were added in just four weeks, and weekly prescriptions as of July 17th were 267,000. Against competition that launched in early April, the Wegovy pill has captured around 90% of the oral obesity medication market.
quarterly_data.figure: 12 weeks to the first 1 million TRx; latest 1 million TRx in four weeks; 267,000 weekly prescriptions as of July 17; around 90% of the oral obesity medication market

quarterly_data.signal: Jamey Millar said the Wegovy pill is expanding the market rather than cannibalizing the injectable: 'we continue to see roughly 80% of patients being GLP-1 treatment naive.' Novo also sees people coming to the Wegovy pill from competitor products and limited cannibalization on injectable Wegovy. CFO Karsten Munk Knudsen added that Novo does not see a lot of direct cannibalization from switching to the Wegovy pill, though indirectly it cannot know how many pill patients would otherwise have started on the injectable.
quarterly_data.figure: roughly 80% of Wegovy pill patients are GLP-1 treatment naive

quarterly_data.signal: Titration and the subscription model. Jamey Millar reported higher dose prescriptions increasing steadily week over week, with more than 20,000 people using the Wegovy pill subscription model for the two higher doses; later in the call he put roughly 30% of prescriptions at the 9 mg and 25 mg strength and 30,000 patients enrolled in the subscription model overall, 20,000 of them Wegovy pill patients. On new starts, many patients start on the 4 mg strength rather than the 1.5 mg start. Rather than cutting list price on the higher doses, Novo prefers 'a targeted surgical solution to that than a universal wholesale change to pricing.'
quarterly_data.figure: more than 20,000 on the two-higher-dose subscription; roughly 30% of prescriptions at 9 mg and 25 mg; 30,000 subscription patients total, 20,000 on the Wegovy pill

quarterly_data.signal: U.S. access remains the constraint. Jamey Millar said 'quality of access for obesity GLP-1s remains poor and is a key focus area' and that while the pill is taken up in the reimbursed commercial channel, the majority of total prescriptions are self-pay. The new Bridge pilot program in Medicare Part D opened the 65+ population with a $50 out-of-pocket copay; eligibility screening, prior authorization and pharmacy navigation 'seems to be going very well' and Novo is 'very pleased with the volume so far,' although whether that is durable and sustainable is yet to be seen. Only a vast minority of today's self-pay business is 65+.
quarterly_data.figure: $50 out-of-pocket copay under the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge program; majority of total prescriptions self-pay

quarterly_data.signal: Jamey Millar sized the U.S. branded obesity market: it 'continues to expand in Q2 2026, growing volumes at around 70% compared to Q2 2025.' The Wegovy franchise continues to lead that market measured on NBRx, with a market share of around 60% during the month of July.
quarterly_data.figure: branded obesity market volumes growing around 70% vs Q2 2025; Wegovy franchise NBRx share around 60% in July

quarterly_data.signal: International Operations EVP Emil Kongshoj Larsen reported GLP-1 sales in International Operations grew by 13% on volume growth and market expansion, with obesity franchise growth of 37%. Novo remains the volume market leader outside the U.S. with around 58% GLP-1 volume market share; that share has been declining over recent quarters but the share of growth 'continues to stabilize,' which management attributes to the step-up approval and launches of Wegovy 7.2 mg and Ozempic 2.0 mg.
quarterly_data.figure: IO GLP-1 sales +13%; IO obesity franchise +37%; around 58% GLP-1 volume market share outside the U.S.

quarterly_data.signal: Ozempic and the high-dose rollout outside the U.S. Emil Kongshoj Larsen said Ozempic 'continues to see solid sales momentum, with sales growth of 10% in the second quarter,' partially driven by Ozempic 2.0 mg, now launched in around 10 countries with good uptake, plus strong Ozempic performance across key European markets. Wegovy 7.2 mg in a single-dose pen is now broadly available in the U.K., where GLP-1 market share has increased since the step-up data, and the 7.2 mg single-dose pen was recently approved in the EU with the first EU market launches planned during Q3.
quarterly_data.figure: Ozempic sales growth 10% in Q2; Ozempic 2.0 mg launched in around 10 countries; Wegovy 7.2 mg single-dose pen EU launches in Q3

quarterly_data.signal: Semaglutide loss of exclusivity has begun. Emil Kongshoj Larsen said 'we saw the first generic entries in the early LOE markets. While modest so far, the LOE impact is expected to be back-end loaded in the second half of 2026.' Karsten Munk Knudsen identified those markets as Canada and Brazil mainly. Novo sees the market expanding in the early LOE countries, driven by more products available at lower prices and significant promotional investments by new entrants, and although generic players have started to capture market share, Novo has so far been able to grow its absolute volumes. In Canada the leading tactic is the savings card program, with good volume retention for both Ozempic and Wegovy in the cash and private insurance channels.
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure

quarterly_data.signal: Wegovy pill rollout outside the U.S. Emil Kongshoj Larsen framed the U.K. headroom: it is estimated that around 20 million adults live with obesity in the U.K. while only around 1.6 million people were treated with obesity medication prior to launch, and 'almost three out of 10 obesity patients on a once weekly GLP-1 and IO live in the U.K.' He attributed the pent-up demand to a real injection barrier and to the pill's lack of drug-drug interactions, which lets patients on oral contraceptives and statins start easily. In the U.A.E. the Wegovy pill became available in early June, roughly one month after an oral competitor entered, and has already captured around 50% market share in the oral segment. Germany follows in September: a different, telehealth-driven market where more than half of the growth and a third of the market is already sold through telehealth channels.
quarterly_data.figure: U.K. around 20 million adults with obesity vs around 1.6 million treated; almost three out of 10 IO once-weekly obesity patients are in the U.K.; U.A.E. around 50% oral-segment share; Germany telehealth is more than half of growth and a third of the market

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Karsten Munk Knudsen walked the balance-of-year and 2027 run-rate bridge. First-half growth was 2%; from that run rate, factor in the loss of exclusivity for semaglutide in a few markets, Canada and Brazil mainly, which happens predominantly in the second half, and the favorable gross-to-net effects of a combined DKK 5 billion booked in Q3 and Q4 last year. The comparative effect does not carry forward into next year while the loss-of-exclusivity impact will annualize into it. On 2027 he declined to guide before February but noted 'the GLP-1 market is growing close to 40%, when we look at moving annual totals' and called out CagriSema's U.S. regulatory action and Mim8's regulatory decision as the swing factors.
quarterly_data.figure: first-half growth 2%; combined DKK 5 billion of favorable prior-year gross-to-net in Q3 and Q4; GLP-1 market growing close to 40% on moving annual totals

quarterly_data.signal: U.S. price and channel mix. Jamey Millar broke down the prior-period gross-to-net adjustment: of the DKK 2 billion highlighted, 'about 3/4 of the impact is Ozempic gross to net, and then the balance is insulin.' On Wegovy injectable he said Novo saw volume growth offset by lower realized prices than anticipated, with no new price dynamic impacting it - 'it's the price dynamic that we started the year with.' Karsten Munk Knudsen added that the business mix has changed: self-pay is now to the tune of 35% of total Wegovy injectable in the U.S., compared to a year ago when it was around the 10%-15% range, at a different price point but a good way to unlock volume.
quarterly_data.figure: DKK 2 billion gross-to-net adjustment, about 3/4 Ozempic and the balance insulin; Wegovy injectable U.S. self-pay around 35% of total vs the 10%-15% range a year ago

quarterly_data.signal: API capacity. Asked where the new API manufacturing facilities stand, Karsten Munk Knudsen said Novo has 'validated the first product in the first finger in the first facility' and that it is progressing very nicely, but that in terms of commercial supply into the marketplace there is 'very low utilization from these facilities, which makes us also bullish in terms of being able to supply significant volumes in the years to come, especially for the Wegovy pill for ex-U.S. rollout.'
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure

quarterly_data.signal: REIMAGINE 4 head-to-head readout. CSO Martin Holst Lange said the completed open-label trial of CagriSema 2.4 mg versus tirzepatide 15 mg produced a weight loss of 15.2% and an HbA1c of 1.9 percentage points at 68 weeks; on the dual primary endpoint CagriSema demonstrated non-inferiority versus tirzepatide for weight reduction but not for HbA1c reduction. He defended the positioning by noting that across the CagriSema diabetes trials HbA1c lowering has run between -1.8% and 2.3%, alongside an 'almost unprecedented 15% weight loss' in diabetes and a 23% weight loss in obesity, plus benefits on blood pressure, glycemic control, lipids and potential bone preservation from amylin biology.
quarterly_data.figure: REIMAGINE 4: 15.2% weight loss and HbA1c of 1.9 percentage points at 68 weeks vs tirzepatide 15 mg; CagriSema diabetes HbA1c lowering between -1.8% and 2.3%; 23% weight loss in obesity

quarterly_data.signal: CagriSema dose-range program. Martin Holst Lange said Novo completed REDEFINE 9, a 68-week efficacy and safety trial testing CagriSema maintenance doses of 1.0 mg and 1.7 mg of each component in people with overweight obesity, where both lower doses achieved superior weight loss compared to placebo and CagriSema appeared safe and well-tolerated; detailed data come later this year. Novo also initiated the CagriSema phase III-B REDEFINE high-dose trial of 2.4 mg cagrilintide plus 7.2 mg semaglutide, comprising two substudies - obesity without diabetes, and obesity with type 2 diabetes - each measured against CagriSema 2.4 mg of each component and semaglutide 7.2 mg alone. He pointed to REDEFINE 11 as the trial testing individualized titration and dosing.
quarterly_data.figure: REDEFINE 9: 68 weeks, CagriSema 1.0 mg and 1.7 mg maintenance doses, superior weight loss vs placebo; REDEFINE high dose: 2.4 mg cagrilintide plus 7.2 mg semaglutide in two substudies

quarterly_data.signal: Pipeline initiations beyond CagriSema. Martin Holst Lange said Novo initiated a phase II trial of its triple agonist targeting GLP-1, GIP and amylin receptors, evaluating different dose escalation regimens for up to 39 weeks and expected to read out in the second half of 2027, plus a phase II trial of once-weekly UBT251 in type 2 diabetes for up to 40 weeks expected to read out by the end of 2027. Planned starts include oral zenagamtide in obesity, cagrilintide high dose, AMBITION - the phase III development program for zenagamtide - and REIMAGINE SWITCH, which evaluates switching from semaglutide 1.0 mg and 2.0 mg to CagriSema with results anticipated in the second half of 2027. Phase III safety results from the SYNCHRONY Real-World trial of efruxifermin in people with MASH and fibrosis stages F1 to F4 are anticipated in the remainder of 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: triple agonist phase II up to 39 weeks, readout second half of 2027; UBT251 phase II up to 40 weeks, readout by end of 2027; REIMAGINE SWITCH results second half of 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Oral franchise strategy. Martin Holst Lange said the completed 50 mg oral semaglutide study 'showed some really good results on both efficacy and tolerability,' but 'at this point in time, we do not see a need to launch the 50 mg' because with the approved 25 mg 'we come out with 17% weight loss and the best tolerability profile as far as we can see in the oral space,' and because Novo has oral zenagamtide plus three more oral assets in its current pipeline and portfolio. On zenagamtide he noted phase II showed 24% weight loss in a matter of six months treatment in obesity, and that it will be offered as both a subcutaneous injection and an oral, taking a further step up in efficacy for oral treatment.
quarterly_data.figure: oral semaglutide 25 mg: 17% weight loss; zenagamtide phase II: 24% weight loss in six months; three more oral assets in the pipeline

quarterly_data.signal: ZEUS safety detail and what happens to the inflammation strategy. Martin Holst Lange said the trial randomized patients in a 1:1 ratio to once-monthly ziltivekimab 15 mg or placebo on top of standard of care, with eligibility requiring high-sensitivity C-reactive protein equal to or above 2 mg per liter. Overall rates of adverse events and serious adverse events were similar between arms, but consistent with targeting IL-6 inhibition a higher proportion of ziltivekimab-treated people had serious infections compared to placebo. He said Novo had 'communicated an effect size of around 50% or less because we acknowledge the risk,' argued the CANTOS trial's IL-1 beta result means inflammation in cardiovascular disease should still be addressed, and said Novo has an NLRP3 asset in phase I plus additional NLRP3 assets in its pre-clinical pipeline that it intends to progress.
quarterly_data.figure: ziltivekimab 15 mg once-monthly, 1:1 randomization, hsCRP equal to or above 2 mg per liter; effect size communicated at around 50% or less

quarterly_data.signal: Business development posture. Mike Doustdar said he does not measure ambition 'by the number or the size of the acquisition we make' and that Novo is focused on bolt-ons that complement internal R&D - 'I've also said we are in every data room' - while a transformative M&A would require Novo to be in a very different situation than it is today. On where he is hunting: Novo sees obesity as 'not a single disease, but multiple conditions with 1 billion people suffering from it differently,' first segmenting the population into injectable versus orals, then looking at adjacent biologies - amylin, GIP and glucagon - that Novo understands scientifically and can manufacture and commercialize the way it does today.
quarterly_data.figure: 1 billion people living with obesity

quarterly_data.quarter: Novo Nordisk press release: Novo's CagriSema delivers superior weight loss versus (09-21-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Topline phase 3 results for once-weekly CagriSema (cagrilintide + semaglutide), highlighted at Novo's Capital Markets Day. REIMAGINE 5 (adults with type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled on metformin, an SGLT2 inhibitor or both): CagriSema 1.0 mg/1.0 mg achieved superior weight loss of 12.4% vs 9.1% for tirzepatide 5 mg and non-inferior HbA1c reduction (1.71% vs 1.67%) at week 60. REDEFINE 9 (overweight or obesity): CagriSema 1.0 mg/1.0 mg delivered 21.0% weight reduction vs 2.0% for placebo at week 68, meeting the primary superiority endpoint. CagriSema was well tolerated overall in both trials. The U.S. NDA for CagriSema in weight management, filed in December 2025, has a decision expected in Q4 2026. Novo also presented first data in painful diabetic neuropathy in type 2 diabetes, with details to come later.
quarterly_data.figure: REIMAGINE 5: weight loss 12.4% vs 9.1% (tirzepatide 5 mg), HbA1c 1.71% vs 1.67% at week 60; REDEFINE 9: 21.0% vs 2.0% placebo at week 68; FDA decision expected Q4 2026

quarterly_data.quarter: Novo Nordisk press release: Highlights to be presented at Novo's Capital Markets Day (09-21-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: At its Capital Markets Day in London, Novo set strategic ambitions for 2030 (by 2030 from a 2026 baseline; the company states they are inherently uncertain and do not constitute its financial outlook or guidance): launch >5 multi-blockbusters by 2030 and deliver >150 bDKK risk-adjusted pipeline sales in 2035; enter or complete ≥ 5 Phase 3 programmes in obesity and diabetes and ≥ 5 in other therapy areas; deliver 2026-30 revenue CAGR in line with industry peers (Eli Lilly, AstraZeneca, Roche and others named); scale capacity to be able to serve 10x more people with obesity on oral GLP-1; serve >60m patients globally by 2030; maintain a broadly stable operating margin and an attractive dividend per share. The revenue and margin ambitions are based on adjusted metrics.
quarterly_data.figure: >5 multi-blockbusters by 2030; >150 bDKK pipeline sales in 2035; ≥ 5 + ≥ 5 Phase 3 programmes; capacity for 10x more oral GLP-1 obesity patients; >60m patients by 2030

quarterly_data.quarter: Novo Nordisk press release: Novo's once-weekly Sogroya (somapacitan) receives positive (09-18-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: The EMA's CHMP recommended once-weekly Sogroya (somapacitan) for children with idiopathic short stature (ISS) with persistent growth disturbance, based on the REAL8 trial (non-inferior to once-daily growth hormone on mean annualised height velocity at Week 52). This follows the May 2026 CHMP recommendation for short stature in children born small for gestational age and with Noonan Syndrome; a European Commission decision on marketing authorisation covering all three indications is expected later this year. ISS affects up to 3% of children worldwide. The company says that, if approved, Sogroya would be the first and only growth hormone treatment approved for ISS in the EU (company claim).
quarterly_data.figure: CHMP positive opinion for ISS; EC decision on three indications expected later this year; ISS up to 3% of children

quarterly_data.quarter: Novo Nordisk press release: Novo: CHMP recommends EU approval of FREHEMGO (denecimig), (09-17-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: The EMA's CHMP adopted a positive opinion recommending EU marketing authorisation for FREHEMGO (denecimig), a factor VIIIa mimetic bispecific antibody given under the skin as routine prophylaxis for haemophilia A with or without inhibitors in adults and children, with once-monthly, once-every-two-weeks and once-weekly dosing in a single-use pre-filled pen; the company calls it the first FVIIIa mimetic to offer these three dosing options (company claim). The opinion is based on the FRONTIER programme: in the pivotal FRONTIER 2 trial denecimig significantly reduced the annualised bleeding rate versus prior clotting-factor prophylaxis and on-demand treatment, FRONTIER 3 in children younger than 12 years was consistent, mean annualised bleeding rates were generally below 1 in the reported phase 3 population, and FRONTIER 5 found no new safety signals on direct switching from emicizumab. Novo expects to launch FREHEMGO in the first European countries in Q4 2026 and broadly across the EU starting early 2027. Denecimig was submitted to the US FDA (BLA) in September 2025. CEO Mike Doustdar called it a differentiated treatment option that can reduce treatment burden.
quarterly_data.figure: CHMP positive opinion; first European launches Q4 2026, broad EU launch from early 2027; mean annualised bleeding rate generally below 1; US BLA submitted September 2025

quarterly_data.quarter: Novo Nordisk press release: Novo and Hengrui Pharma enter exclusive license agreement (09-29-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Licensor Hengrui Pharma: Novo Nordisk entered a license agreement with Hengrui Pharma (600276.SH; 01276.HK) for HRS-1596, a phase 1-ready GLP-1 receptor and GIP receptor dual agonist with potential for once-weekly oral dosing. Novo obtains exclusive rights to develop, manufacture and commercialise HRS-1596 globally, excluding mainland China, Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan. The agreement is subject to U.S. Hart-Scott-Rodino clearance and other customary closing conditions and is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026. CSO Martin Holst Lange: 'we are excited to add HRS-1596 to our growing pipeline and to explore its potential to raise the bar for convenience in the field.'
quarterly_data.figure: exclusive global rights excluding mainland China, Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan; expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Regulatory approvals listed in the H1 2026 financial report that the Q2 call did not detail: in July the European Medicines Agency (EMA) granted approval of Wegovy pill for the treatment of excess body weight and long-term weight management, with SELECT cardiovascular data in the label; the US FDA approved the Wegovy FlexTouch pen for semaglutide 2.4 mg in obesity, with launch expected in the second half of 2026; the US FDA and the EMA approved the manual prefilled syringe (mPFS) device for Wegovy 2.4 mg and for Ozempic 0.25, 0.5 and 1.0 mg doses; Awiqli was approved in the US; and the CHMP gave a positive opinion for adding SUSTAIN OPTIMIZE (Ozempic 2.0 mg as an add-on to dose-reduced insulin glargine) to the EU Ozempic label.
quarterly_data.figure: EMA: Wegovy pill (July); FDA: Wegovy FlexTouch 2.4 mg pen, Awiqli; FDA and EMA: mPFS devices for Wegovy 2.4 mg and Ozempic 0.25, 0.5 and 1.0 mg; CHMP positive opinion: Ozempic SUSTAIN OPTIMIZE label

quarterly_data.quarter: Novo Nordisk press release: Novo's denecimig demonstrates tolerability after switch (09-17-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Phase 3b FRONTIER5 results for denecimig, published in the Journal of Thrombosis and Haemostasis: 61 adults and adolescents aged 12 and older with haemophilia A, with or without inhibitors, switched directly from emicizumab to the denecimig pen without a washout period or loading dose and completed 26 weeks. Primary safety endpoint: 107 treatment-emergent adverse events in 43 patients (70.5%), 98.1% mild to moderate, 24 possibly/probably related; no thromboembolic events, hypersensitivity reactions or discontinuations, and no clinical evidence of neutralising anti-denecimig antibodies. Of 59 patients asked, 98.3% rated the pen easy or very easy to use and 96.6% preferred it to their previous method; treatment burden (Hemo-TEM) fell by an average of 4.7 points from a baseline of 10.5. Exploratory: mean peak thrombin generation rose from 25.5 nmol/L at week 0 to 39.8 nmol/L at week 26 (mean of individual changes 78.8%), into the normal range with no excessive clotting, and steady state was reached by week 16 without a loading dose.

quarterly_data.signal: Company real-world study COMPETE SWITCH CV, presented at EASD 2026: in a retrospective US claims analysis (Komodo Health) of 636,525 adults with type 2 diabetes on semaglutide injection 1 mg, those who escalated to Ozempic 2 mg were associated with a statistically significant 6% lower risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (all-cause death, heart attack, stroke) than those who switched to tirzepatide up to 15 mg (Adjusted HR 1.06; 95% CI 1.04-1.08; P=0.005), with a consistent result in a subset with baseline HbA1c / weight data (Adjusted HR 1.07, 95% CI 1.01-1.13). The CV analysis included 185,705 adults who escalated to semaglutide 2 mg and 23,104 who switched to tirzepatide. Within 365 days, 67.2% remained on semaglutide 1 mg, 29.2% escalated to 2 mg and 3.6% switched to tirzepatide (at 720 days: 57.4%, 36.9% and 5.7%). Safety outcomes were not assessed; the company notes real-world analyses show associations, not causality.

The company notes real-world studies evaluate associations and cannot determine causality, and that persistence was required (possible selection bias) and weights were self-reported. quarterly_data.quarter: Novo Nordisk press release: Novo's Wegovy (semaglutide) reduced liver fat to normal (10-01-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Post hoc exploratory analysis of the phase 3b STEP UP trials presented at EASD 2026 (not a pre-specified primary or secondary endpoint): in a STEP UP sub-population of 55 adults with obesity without diabetes whose liver fat was measured by MRI-PDFF, mean liver fat on Wegovy (pooled semaglutide 7.2 and 2.4 mg) declined from 8.8% at baseline to 3.1% at week 72; of the 26 participants who entered with liver fat above 5%, 88.5% (23 participants) reached the below-5% normal threshold by week 72. The release states Wegovy (semaglutide 2.4 mg) is approved for the treatment of MASH in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, China and several other markets; semaglutide 7.2 mg is not being investigated for MASH, and results from part 2 of the ongoing phase 3 ESSENCE MASH trial (1,197 participants, 240 weeks) are expected in 2029.

quarterly_data.quarter: Tempus AI press release: Tempus Study Published in Nature Medicine Demonstrates (08-04-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Tempus announced study results, published in Nature Medicine, showing that PRISM2, a multimodal slide-level pathology foundation model developed in collaboration with researchers from Microsoft, can perform clinically important diagnostic tasks using simple prompts: PRISM2 outperformed or matched existing slide-level foundation models across a comprehensive set of diagnostic, biomarker and patient outcome prediction tasks, and when further tuned to predict long-term outcomes it outperformed standalone models, including achieving high performance predicting colorectal cancer recurrence-free survival. quarterly_data.signal: The company announced publication in The Lancet Neurology of what it calls the first longitudinal cohort study to evaluate a broad panel of plasma biomarkers in patients receiving anti-amyloid antibody therapy (lecanemab) in real-world clinical practice. Led by Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis investigators, the study used Alamar's NULISAseq CNS 120 panel to measure 130 plasma proteins, profiling 2,385 samples from 1,967 participants with just 25 microliters of plasma per sample. Results stated by the company: proteins associated with amyloid clearance were largely different from those associated with subsequent cognitive decline; among 197 lecanemab-treated patients, 34 of the 130 biomarkers significantly changed with the number of infusions, not all in the same direction; and brain-derived forms of tau consistently outperformed the same proteins circulating in the periphery, accounting for four of the top five proteins distinguishing these patients from controls both before treatment and at the last infusion stage. The company says measuring these variants alongside more than 100 additional proteins in a single sample is what allowed the investigators to track pathology and treatment response in one assay. CEO: the study shows why measuring one or two biomarkers is not enough to understand treatment and why ultra-high sensitivity matters.

Safety: 15 of 18 (84.2%) treatment-related AEs were Grade 1/2, Grade 3 in 15.8% of patients, no Grade 4/5 events, 4 discontinuations. REC-4881 (oral MEK1/2 inhibitor, FAP), Chief Development Officer Vicki Goodman: in the ongoing Phase II TUPELO study, post-colectomy FAP patients receiving REC-4881 showed a median polyp burden reduction of 43% after three months of treatment; the effect was durable, with sustained reductions after three months off treatment, and reductions were seen in both duodenal (upper GI) and lower GI disease - approximately 90% of FAP patients develop upper GI polyps. The safety profile is manageable with predominantly mild to moderate adverse events, consistent with other MEK inhibitors. TUPELO continues to enroll, including patients 18 years of age and older and a dose optimization cohort. The data were first presented in December via a webinar; she said FDA engagement focuses on de-risking the study design, including the appropriate primary endpoint, given very limited regulatory precedent in FAP.

REC-7735 is designed to be greater than 100-fold selective for H1047R; the go decision rested on preclinical efficacy similar to or improved on competitor profiles, lack of hyperglycemia and GLP tox studies. quarterly_data.quarter: Absci press release: Absci Announces Preliminary Details for Phase 2 STORYLINE (09-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Absci announced additional details for its planned global, multi-center Phase 2 STORYLINE trial of ABS-201, an investigational anti-prolactin receptor (PRLR) antibody engineered with its generative AI platform, for endometriosis. The planned double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial would assess efficacy and safety in participants with surgically-diagnosed endometriosis and moderate to severe endometriosis-associated pain after a run-in period, with efficacy endpoints including reductions in dysmenorrhea and non-menstrual pelvic pain. Absci anticipates recruiting approximately 150 patients from approximately 10 or more countries, subject to protocol finalization and regulatory clearance, and anticipates initiation in mid-2027. It is designed as a dose-ranging trial, anticipating testing two or three dose levels to be confirmed following review of data from the ongoing HEADLINE trial.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately 150 patients; approximately 10 or more countries; anticipated initiation mid-2027; two or three dose levels

quarterly_data.quarter: AbCellera press release: AbCellera Announces Positive Top-Line Phase 2 Clinical (08-10-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Positive top-line results from the Phase 2 portion of the Phase 1/2 trial of ABCL635, an investigational NK3R antagonist antibody developed as a non-hormonal, long-acting, subcutaneous treatment for moderate-to-severe vasomotor symptoms (VMS) due to menopause: the study met its primary efficacy endpoints, with statistically significant reductions in both frequency and severity at week 4 versus placebo after a single dose. The randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter study enrolled 92 postmenopausal women with a mean of approximately 10 moderate or severe hot flashes per day, randomized 1:1 to a single subcutaneous 600 mg dose or placebo. Frequency: an 8.8 mean reduction in moderate and severe events per day from baseline at week 4 (Day 29) versus 3.5 for placebo, a mean placebo-adjusted difference of 5.3 (p<0.001); mean percent reduction 83% versus 33%, a placebo-adjusted difference of 50%. Severity: a mean reduction of 1.4 points versus 0.3, a placebo-adjusted difference of 1.1 (p<0.001); 58% versus 12%, a placebo-adjusted difference of 46%. Statistical significance was maintained from week 1 through week 4, and ABCL635 significantly improved sleep and patient global impression of change. It was well tolerated over the four weeks with no serious adverse events, severe adverse events or adverse events leading to discontinuation; the most common adverse events above placebo were headache, fatigue and injection site reaction. AbCellera calls the reductions best-in-class.
quarterly_data.figure: 92 patients; frequency reduction 8.8 vs 3.5 events per day (difference 5.3, p<0.001; 83% vs 33%); severity reduction 1.4 vs 0.3 (difference 1.1, p<0.001; 58% vs 12%)

He does not think a direct head-to-head trial against the small molecules is needed to convince patients or caregivers; it may have value in pricing discussions and could be run as a side study after the registrational trials. He thinks the efficacy is 'highly unlikely to miss' in Phase III ('we are very bullish on that'). quarterly_data.signal: GB-0895 Phase 1 asthma results (ERS poster furnished on 8-K; study GB-0895-101, unblinded Parts A and B, data cutoff 26Jan2026): 80 participants with mild-to-moderate asthma in the single-ascending-dose part (10 mg to 1200 mg, 3:1 vs placebo) and 16 in the multiple-ascending-dose part (300 mg or 600 mg Q12W x 2). GB-0895 was well tolerated with no treatment-related SAEs: any TEAE 66 (95.7%) on GB-0895 vs 26 (96.3%) on placebo, any serious TEAE 1 (1.4%) vs 2 (7.4%), injection-site reactions 10 (14.5%) vs 4 (14.8%), all ISRs Grade 1; the 3 SAEs (1 GB-0895, 2 placebo) were all Grade 3 and none related to GB-0895. PK was sustained and dose-proportional with a half-life of about 98 days at 300 mg, with no evidence of target-mediated drug disposition or of anti-drug antibodies affecting half-life. The poster concludes that 300 mg achieves maximal suppression of the PD biomarkers BEC, FeNO, IL-5 and IL-13 for at least 6 months, that doses above 300 mg show no meaningful improvement, and that a single subcutaneous 300 mg injection exhibits broad anti-inflammatory activity for at least 6 months, supporting a dosing regimen of one subcutaneous injection every 6 months. Generate designed GB-0895 with ~20-fold higher affinity for TSLP than tezepelumab and YTE Fc modifications for extended half-life (company claim).
